_comment: Hand-authored featured content of the SIG part, transcribed from the ISCA SIG Atlas public page (2026-08-31, QA-fixed version). The SIG directory data itself lives in sigs.json (regenerate with scripts/import_sigs.mjs). Dates and 'coming up' rows are a snapshot as of the review date below.
part_blurb: The second half of SCOOT 2.0: what each of ISCA's 20 Special Interest Groups is doing — workshops, challenges, journals — and, front and centre, every webinar and lecture series with video recordings that could be confirmed. Every link in this part was reviewed on 31 August 2026 against the linked page or a first-party source.
series_intro: Recurring online series run by the SIGs themselves. Five are currently live; two are paused but keep their recording archives online; one is announced but has not yet published a schedule or recordings.

series.name: SPSC Webinar & Café
series.cad: monthly webinar + monthly journal-club café · since Jul 2020
series.text: The most complete webinar operation of any SIG: a full recording index back to July 2020, most talks on YouTube, some on EURECOM's media server.

series.name: Speech Prosody Lectures
series.text: Virtual lecture series with every talk recorded and indexed.
series.next: Upcoming: Xiaoming Jiang (Sep 4), Peggy Mok (Oct 21), Sacha Calhoun (Nov 17).

series.name: SIGML Virtual Seminar Series
series.text: Machine-learning-for-speech seminars: ran Apr–Dec 2021, resumed strongly in 2025 (latest: Charles McGhee, 14 Nov 2025). All recordings indexed on the seminar page.

series.name: SLaTE Webinar Series
series.text: Speech-and-language-in-education talks, live-streamed and archived on the SIG's own YouTube channel.

series.name: SIGSLT Seminars
series.text: Spoken-language-translation talk series; per-talk recording links on the lectures page, plus a channel playlist. No talks since May 2023.

series.name: Présente Tes Recherches
series.text: Research-presentation series by JCeP, AFCP's young-researchers group; sessions #6–#9 recorded and published. No new recordings since July 2023.

series.name: AISV online courses & OLF
series.text: Live online courses (via Teams, no public archive) plus the OLF forensic-linguistics observatory, whose roundtables are recorded — e.g. a Senate event on Radio Radicale.

series.name: SynSIG Online Seminars
series.text: A seminar section exists on the SIG's events page but is still an empty placeholder — no schedule, speakers or recordings yet. One to watch (or nudge).

upcoming_intro: Webinars and SIG events on the calendar. Interspeech 2026 (Sydney) satellites marked ✻.

upcoming.what: Oral sources & archives study day (7th), Milan

archives_intro: One-off and per-edition recordings from SIG flagship events — keynotes, tutorials and full sessions.

archives.name: WiSSAP 2023 — Winter School on Speech & Audio

directory_intro: All 20 SIGs with their reviewed activities and video resources. Expand a card for detail; every link was checked.
central_intro: Association-level resources, for context. Key finding: ISCA has no central YouTube channel — video lives fragmented across per-conference channels, SuperLectures and SIG channels.

central.name: ISCA Video Archive
central.what: The closest thing to a central index: links recorded talks for Interspeech 2010–2022 (SuperLectures per year + per-year YouTube channels), Odyssey 2010–2016, ISCSLP 2014 and several keynote lectures. It indexes externally hosted video rather than hosting any — and it currently stops at 2022.

central.name: Per-conference Interspeech YouTube channels
central.what: Each Interspeech organizing committee creates its own channel — the 2021 channel includes the ISCA Medalist lecture, the 2022 channel the keynotes. Older channels are listed on the Video Archive page.

central.name: Speech Pitch — the ISCA-SAC podcast
central.what: Student Advisory Committee interview series, 24+ episodes (Hermansky & Morgan, “Behind the Scenes at ISCA”, Interspeech 2026 preview…).

central.name: ISCA Distinguished Lecturers
central.what: Per a March 2026 board decision the programme moves to online lectures (2026–27 lecturers: Joseph Keshet, Kong Aik Lee, Kai Yu). No recording archive announced yet — the natural future home for association-level recorded lectures.

central.name: ISCA International Virtual Seminars
central.what: A speaker pool (18+ experts) that labs can invite for online talks — arranged lab-to-speaker; no public recording archive.

central.name: SCOOT — the original guide to online training resources
central.what: ISCA's curated directory of third-party learning resources in speech communication, including video lecture courses; a directory, it hosts nothing itself. The catalog in the first half of this page is a rebuild and extension of it.

central.name: ISCA Archive
central.what: 40,000+ papers from 398 events (1970–2026) — papers and abstracts only, no video.

notes.text: synsig.org is a hijacked domain — SynSIG's historical address now serves a gambling site. Do not link it anywhere; the SIG's real home is now on isca-speech.org.
The ISCA Video Archive stops at 2022 — three years of Interspeech / workshop video links are missing from the association's own index.
SynSIG's “Online Seminars” section is an empty placeholder — announced but never launched; a nudge to the new officer team could unlock a sixth live SIG series.
4 of 20 SIGs have no located recordings at all (AVISA, SIG-CHILD, SIG-IL, SIGRU) — AVSP 2026 in October is a natural moment for AVISA to start recording.
Former SIGs SALTMIL and SLIM are listed as historical (“Old SIGs”) on the official page and are not counted here.

Where a SIG went quiet, its recordings usually survive on personal or host-institution channels (SIGML → an officer's channel; SSW11 → the Hungarian host; WiSSAP → an IIT Kanpur lab) — a continuity risk worth noting.

method: The SIG part was compiled 31 August 2026 from the official ISCA SIG list, each SIG's own website, and targeted searches. Every video link was reviewed. Most were fetched directly; links blocked by consent walls, bot protection, or broken TLS were checked through first-party index pages, direct video metadata, or YouTube oEmbed and are described with their verification limits. A second, independent pass re-checked every link and actively searched for recordings the first pass might have missed; one dead video link was removed.
disclosure: The ISCA SIGs & online events part of this page is an independent reference, not an official ISCA publication. It was researched and compiled by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of an ISCA board member. Facts reflect what the linked sources stated on 31 August 2026; corrections welcome.
